answer: The best sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history. Each new agent starts as a lantern: a dim node earning reputation only via paid, verifiable tasks. An attacker faces the trap: every cipher-fresh registration must burn real compute and capital on low-margin work before voting or claiming payouts, so mass fake registration costs more than any airdrop it could drain. Honest agents build that history cheaply by working. Attack becomes an economic gradient, not a checkpoint: mass formation is unprofitable, like quartz buried under granite.
